prompt: A teammate opened a PR with a small capacity-estimation snippet used to justify picking a datastore for a new service: it takes daily traffic inputs, derives an average QPS, multiplies by a hardcoded peak factor to get peakQps (the example run in the PR description lands peakQps at about 2145), and then decides the whole architecture with one global if-branch — over 1000 QPS means a distributed store, otherwise a single relational node — while also projecting a 10-year storage figure straight from record count times record size. Review this PR out loud as you would in a real code review: what do you flag as a blocker, what is merely a stylistic nitpick, and what would you propose instead?
